issue_title: TSDB WAL replay OOM on large WAL segments after unclean shutdown
issue_body: Prometheus OOMs during WAL replay when the WAL contains segments larger than 128MB created during a write surge before an unclean shutdown. The replay process loads the entire segment into memory before applying records instead of streaming records incrementally. On systems with 8GB of RAM a 512MB WAL segment causes an OOM kill before the replay completes leaving Prometheus unable to restart. The fix requires a streaming WAL reader implementation in tsdb/wal/reader.go. This is a critical reliability issue for high-ingestion deployments.

issue_title: Store Gateway block sync fails silently for partially uploaded blocks in object store
issue_body: The Thanos Store Gateway silently skips blocks that are partially uploaded to the object store instead of logging an error or alerting. This causes gaps in query coverage that are not visible to operators. A partially uploaded block occurs when an uploader crashes mid-upload which is a common failure mode. The block index file is present but some chunk files are missing. The Store Gateway should detect this state explicitly and expose it as a metric. This has caused silent data gaps in our long-term metrics storage discovered only during an incident.

issue_title: Watch event ordering not guaranteed when compaction runs concurrently with watch resumption
issue_body: etcd does not guarantee watch event ordering when a compaction operation runs concurrently with a watch resumption triggered by an ErrCompacted error. The watch client resumes from the compacted revision but some events in the range between the old watch revision and the compaction revision may be delivered out of order or dropped. This violates the watch ordering guarantee documented in the etcd API specification. We have reproduced this with a test that triggers compaction precisely when the watch client is processing the ErrCompacted and resuming.

issue_title: VTGate connection spike during primary failover with connection pool warm-up race
issue_body: During a primary tablet failover VTGate experiences a connection spike that exceeds the configured pool size limit because multiple goroutines simultaneously attempt to warm up the connection pool to the new primary. The connection pool warm-up is not coordinated across goroutines leading to transient overload on the new primary that can delay failover completion. In our 100-shard setup this causes a 10-15 second degradation during planned failovers. The fix requires a single-flight pattern on the pool warm-up path.

issue_title: Actor reminder fires multiple times when placement table update races with reminder scheduling
issue_body: Dapr actor reminders fire multiple times when a placement table update occurs during the reminder scheduling window. The double-fire is caused by a race between the placement service updating the actor-to-host mapping and the reminder scheduler checking if the current host is authoritative for the actor. Two hosts transiently believe they are authoritative and both schedule the reminder. This causes duplicate side effects in workflows where reminder idempotency is not enforced. The fix requires a distributed lock or fencing token during the placement transition.

issue_title: Remote cache poisoning via non-hermetic action that leaks hostname into output
issue_body: A non-hermetic Bazel action that leaks the build machine hostname into a compiled artifact can poison the remote action cache with machine-specific outputs. Subsequent builds on different machines retrieve the poisoned cache entry and use the incorrect artifact without any cache miss signal. This is a correctness and security issue in environments with a shared remote cache. The action sandbox should either prevent hostname access or include the hostname as part of the cache key. We have reproduced this with a C++ action that embeds file paths.

issue_title: TraceContext propagation broken across thread pool boundaries with virtual threads
issue_body: OpenTelemetry Java context propagation fails to correctly propagate TraceContext across thread pool boundaries when Java 21 virtual threads are used. The Context.current() call in the child virtual thread returns an empty context instead of the parent thread context. This causes distributed traces to be broken at every async boundary implemented with virtual threads. The ContextStorage implementation is not compatible with virtual thread semantics. This is a blocking issue for adopters migrating to Java 21 virtual threads.

issue_title: Application sync wave ordering violated when resource hook fails and retry occurs
issue_body: Argo CD violates sync wave ordering when a resource hook in an intermediate wave fails and the sync operation retries. On retry the application controller re-evaluates all waves from wave 0 instead of resuming from the failed wave hook. Resources in earlier waves that are already healthy are re-synced unnecessarily and resources in later waves may be synced before the failed hook is retried in the correct order. This causes transient inconsistency during sync operations with hooks. The wave ordering state needs to be persisted across retry attempts.

issue_title: Kustomization reconciliation loop detected incorrectly when ConfigMap checksum changes
issue_body: Flux2 Kustomization controller incorrectly detects a reconciliation loop when a ConfigMap part of the Kustomization has its checksum annotation updated by an external process. The controller interprets the external update as a conflicting write from a previous reconciliation cycle and enters a backoff state. This causes legitimate ConfigMap updates to be reverted by subsequent reconciliations. The issue is in the drift detection logic which uses the last-applied-configuration annotation as the sole source of truth without considering external mutations.

issue_title: Cluster provisioning stuck in updating state when cloud provider quota exceeded silently
issue_body: Rancher cluster provisioning gets stuck in the updating state indefinitely when the underlying cloud provider returns a quota exceeded error during node group scaling. The error is not surfaced in the Rancher UI or logs beyond a generic timeout message. The cluster remains in updating state until manually deleted and recreated. The provisioning controller should detect quota exceeded errors from the cloud provider API and surface them as a clear user-facing error condition with actionable guidance. This affects EKS and GKE provisioners.

issue_title: Composition revision upgrade causes managed resource ownership conflict with external name annotation
issue_body: Upgrading a Composition revision while managed resources are actively being reconciled causes an ownership conflict when the new revision changes the external-name annotation strategy. The managed resources created by the old revision are not correctly transferred to the new revision ownership causing the new revision reconciler to attempt to create duplicate resources in the cloud provider. This results in cloud provider API errors and stuck composite resources. The revision upgrade process needs a migration phase that transfers ownership before applying new annotation strategies.

issue_title: Node consolidation incorrectly evicts pods with local storage when storageClass allows migration
issue_body: Karpenter node consolidation logic incorrectly evicts pods that use local storage PersistentVolumeClaims even when the StorageClass has a volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer policy that permits migration to a new node. The consolidation eviction logic checks for local storage usage but does not consult the StorageClass binding mode to determine if the PVC can be rescheduled. This causes unnecessary eviction failures and prevents consolidation of nodes with migratable local storage workloads.

issue_title: Policy evaluation non-deterministic with concurrent partial evaluation cache writes
issue_body: OPA exhibits non-deterministic policy evaluation results when partial evaluation is enabled and multiple concurrent requests write to the partial evaluation cache simultaneously. The cache write operation is not atomic and concurrent writes can result in a partially updated cache entry being read by a subsequent request. This produces incorrect authorization decisions that are not reproducible. We observed this in production under 5000 req/s load with partial evaluation enabled. The cache implementation in rego/eval.go requires a read-write mutex on cache entries.

issue_title: Rule engine regex compilation blocks event processing under high syscall rate
issue_body: The Falco rule engine recompiles regex patterns for each rule evaluation when a kernel event matches the rule syscall filter. Under a high syscall rate exceeding 100k events per second this causes the rule engine thread to spend the majority of its CPU time on regex compilation rather than event evaluation. The compiled regex patterns should be cached after first compilation and reused. The current architecture in engine/rule_engine.cpp constructs a new RE2 object for each event evaluation. This causes a 40% CPU overhead in our production environment.

issue_title: Message deduplication false positives under producer restart with sequence ID reset
issue_body: Apache Pulsar message deduplication mechanism produces false positives when a producer restarts and resets its sequence ID to 0. The broker incorrectly identifies the first message after restart as a duplicate of a historical message with the same producer name and sequence ID 0. This causes legitimate messages to be silently dropped. The deduplication store should include the producer epoch in the deduplication key to distinguish messages from different producer lifetimes. This is a data loss bug.

issue_title: Read restart error not correctly retried in implicit transaction for complex joins
issue_body: YugabyteDB read restart error handling does not correctly retry implicit transactions that involve complex multi-table joins when the read restart is triggered midway through join execution. The retry logic restarts the transaction but does not correctly invalidate the partially computed join result leading to either incorrect results or a second read restart error that is surfaced to the client. This violates the serializable isolation guarantee. We observed this with 5-table star schema queries under high write concurrency.

issue_title: Tracing policy drops events silently when ring buffer backpressure exceeds threshold
issue_body: Tetragon tracing policy silently drops kernel events when the eBPF ring buffer experiences backpressure beyond a configurable threshold. The dropped events are not counted in any exported metric making it impossible for operators to determine if their tracing coverage is complete. The ring buffer drop counter in the kernel is not mapped to a Prometheus metric. This is a significant observability gap for security monitoring use cases where event completeness is critical. We need a tetragon_events_dropped_total metric labeled by policy and event type.

issue_title: Machine config apply fails silently for invalid network device selector with no matching interfaces
issue_body: Applying a Talos machine configuration with a network device selector that matches no physical interfaces fails silently. The configuration is accepted and the machine appears healthy but the intended network configuration is never applied. The correct behavior should be to reject the configuration with a validation error listing the expected selectors and the available interfaces. This causes silent network misconfiguration that is only discovered when network connectivity fails. The validation logic in the config controller does not check device selector resolution at apply time.

issue_title: Shadow indexing S3 upload stalls when AWS SDK connection pool is exhausted under burst writes
issue_body: Redpanda shadow indexing feature stalls S3 segment uploads when the AWS SDK connection pool is exhausted during a write burst. The upload stall is not surfaced as an error and the segment upload queue grows unboundedly consuming heap memory until OOM. The S3 client should implement a bounded queue with backpressure signaling to the partition leadership. Currently the upload path in src/v/cloud_storage/remote.cc does not apply any admission control before enqueuing S3 operations.

issue_title: Raft log compaction races with snapshot generation causing follower log gap
issue_body: TiKV Raft log compaction can race with snapshot generation on the leader causing a follower to receive a snapshot that refers to a log index that has already been compacted on the leader. The follower then has a log gap between its applied index and the snapshot included index which it cannot recover from without manual intervention. This is a data availability issue in clusters with slow followers. The fix requires coordinating log compaction with in-progress snapshot generation to ensure the snapshot covers all compacted log entries.

issue_title: Materialized view update lag spikes during table repair due to view update queue starvation
issue_body: ScyllaDB materialized view update lag spikes to several minutes during a table repair operation because the repair process and the view update queue compete for the same IO scheduler resources. The repair operation is given higher priority causing the view update queue to be starved for the duration of the repair. This causes queries on the materialized view to return stale data for the duration of the repair window. The IO scheduler should provide separate resource quotas for repair and view update operations.

issue_title: Parallel SQL execution produces non-deterministic results for ORDER BY on floating point columns
issue_body: QuestDB parallel SQL execution engine produces non-deterministic result ordering for ORDER BY queries on floating point columns when the sort key contains NaN values. The parallel merge sort does not define a stable total ordering for NaN values causing different orderings on different runs. This is a correctness issue for analytical queries that rely on deterministic output ordering. The SQL standard defines NaN ordering behavior and QuestDB implementation should conform to it consistently.

issue_title: Kafka rolling update stalls when broker pod anti-affinity prevents scheduling on all nodes
issue_body: The Strimzi Kafka operator stalls a rolling broker update indefinitely when the broker pod anti-affinity rules prevent the replacement pod from being scheduled on any available node in the cluster. The operator does not detect the unschedulable pod condition and simply waits for the pod to become ready. The update should fail fast with a clear error message when the replacement pod cannot be scheduled due to anti-affinity constraints. This has caused extended Kafka unavailability during cluster maintenance windows.

issue_title: Certificate renewal triggers unnecessary TLS connection disruption in high-traffic services
issue_body: cert-manager certificate renewal process triggers an unnecessary rotation of the Kubernetes Secret containing the TLS certificate and private key even when the new certificate has the same key pair. This causes a brief TLS connection disruption in services that watch the Secret for updates because they reload their TLS configuration on any Secret change. cert-manager should only rotate the Secret when the certificate content actually changes and should support issuing new certificates with the existing key pair when configured.

issue_title: System call interception adds measurable latency for high-frequency futex operations
issue_body: gVisor system call interception layer adds 15-20 microseconds of overhead per futex operation compared to native Linux execution. For applications that use futex heavily such as Go runtimes and Java virtual machines this overhead accumulates to a 30-40% overall application slowdown. The futex implementation in gVisor sentry should be optimized to reduce the context switch overhead for uncontested futex operations by implementing a fast path that avoids full kernel entry simulation for the common case.

issue_title: Network partition simulation leaves stale iptables rules after test completion
issue_body: The chaos-toolkit network partition experiment leaves stale iptables rules in place when the experiment is terminated abnormally via SIGKILL or when the rollback phase encounters an error. These stale rules cause persistent network connectivity issues on the test host that persist across chaos experiment runs and require manual cleanup. The experiment rollback handler must be implemented as a registered cleanup handler that executes even on abnormal termination. The current implementation relies on a finally block that does not execute on SIGKILL.

issue_title: ScaledObject metric aggregation uses incorrect time window when multiple triggers are configured
issue_body: KEDA ScaledObject metric aggregation uses the time window of the first trigger to aggregate metrics from all configured triggers when multiple triggers are present. This causes incorrect scaling decisions when different triggers have different cooldown periods. A ScaledObject with a Kafka trigger with 2-minute cooldown and a Prometheus trigger with 30-second cooldown will evaluate both triggers using the 2-minute window causing the Prometheus trigger to react too slowly to metric changes.

issue_title: Machine allocation stuck in provisioning state when Talos version mismatch detected
issue_body: Omni machine allocation process gets stuck in the provisioning state when a Talos version mismatch is detected between the cluster required version and the machine installed version. The version mismatch should trigger an upgrade workflow but instead the allocator waits indefinitely for a condition that can only be resolved by manual intervention. The error is logged at debug level and not surfaced in the Omni UI. A clear user-facing error and an automated upgrade trigger are needed for this case.

issue_title: Pipeline run garbage collection incorrectly deletes runs belonging to different namespaces
issue_body: The Kubeflow Pipelines run garbage collection process has a namespace isolation bug where it can delete pipeline runs from namespaces other than the one it is configured to manage. This occurs when the run name is the same across namespaces and the garbage collector uses name-based matching instead of namespace-qualified unique identifiers. This is a data loss bug with cross-tenant impact in multi-tenant Kubeflow deployments. The fix requires the garbage collector to use the full namespace/name qualified identifier for all run operations.

issue_title: Gang scheduling deadlock when multiple jobs compete for same resource quota simultaneously
issue_body: Volcano gang scheduling implementation deadlocks when multiple jobs simultaneously compete for the same resource quota and each job minimum available pod count is greater than half the available quota slots. The scheduler attempts to allocate resources for all competing jobs simultaneously without a tie-breaking mechanism causing a circular wait where each job holds partial resources needed by the other. This results in all competing jobs being stuck in the Pending state indefinitely.

issue_title: Dev mode file sync corrupts binary files larger than 4MB during incremental sync
issue_body: Nocalhost file synchronization in dev mode corrupts binary files larger than 4MB during incremental sync operations. The corruption is caused by the incremental sync algorithm splitting binary files at arbitrary byte boundaries without awareness of file format structure. Binary files that cross the 4MB chunk boundary have their content incorrectly reassembled on the remote container. The fix requires either a full-file sync for binary files detected by MIME type or a content-addressed chunking algorithm that preserves file integrity.

issue_title: Segment compaction introduces vector index inconsistency under concurrent search
issue_body: Milvus segment compaction introduces a brief period of vector index inconsistency when a compaction merges multiple segments while a concurrent search query is in flight. The search query may return results from the pre-compaction segment layout after the compaction has committed causing stale or missing vectors in the search results. The compaction commit protocol needs to coordinate with the search path using a segment generation counter to ensure searches see a consistent view of the segment layout before and after compaction.

issue_title: Model registry stage transition webhook fires duplicate events on transient DB failures
issue_body: The MLflow model registry fires duplicate stage transition webhook events when the database experiences a transient failure during the transition commit. The webhook delivery is not idempotent and is triggered both on the initial attempt and on the retry after the transient failure is resolved. In production environments with unreliable database connections this causes downstream systems to receive duplicate model deployment triggers. The fix requires idempotency keys on webhook deliveries or deduplication at the delivery layer.

issue_title: Ray cluster scaling blocked when autoscaler pod is evicted during scale-up operation
issue_body: The KubeRay autoscaler pod being evicted during a scale-up operation leaves the Ray cluster in a partially scaled state from which it cannot recover automatically. The new autoscaler pod does not resume the in-progress scale-up operation and instead waits for the next autoscaler trigger. During this recovery window the Ray cluster has fewer nodes than needed causing job failures due to insufficient resources. The autoscaler should persist scale-up intent durably and resume in-progress operations on restart.

issue_title: CloneSet rolling update skips health check when pod readiness gate is not registered
issue_body: OpenKruise CloneSet rolling updates skip the pod readiness gate health check when the readiness gate is configured but the corresponding readiness controller has not registered its condition type in the cluster. Instead of blocking the rollout and alerting the operator the CloneSet proceeds as if the readiness gate is satisfied. This can cause unhealthy pods to be treated as ready during rolling updates leading to brief traffic degradation. The CloneSet controller should validate readiness gate registration before starting a rolling update.

issue_title: Certificate rotation fails silently for etcd peer certificates when etcd is external
issue_body: kubeadm certs renew silently succeeds without actually rotating etcd peer certificates when etcd is configured as an external cluster. The command reports success but the external etcd peer certificates are not updated. The rotation code path checks for the presence of the etcd client certificate on the local node and exits early when not found without distinguishing between a managed and an external etcd configuration. This causes the external etcd peer certificates to expire without warning.

issue_title: PodChaos experiment continues after target pod is deleted and recreated with same name

The experiment target matching uses only the pod name without validating the pod UID which is unique across pod lifecycle events. This can cause unintended fault injection into a replacement production pod if the experiment was intended only for the original pod instance.

issue_title: eBPF probe attachment fails silently on kernel 6.6 due to BTF type ID mismatch

The probes appear to load successfully but produce no data. The error is logged only at trace level making it invisible in standard deployments. The probe attachment should validate that the BTF type IDs match the expected structure layout after loading and surface a clear error when they do not.
